credits.source: Geometric Design: Working With 6 and 12 (Dodecagram Pattern)
credits.creator: Envato Tuts+
credits.note: The pattern of two six-pointed stars in each circle of the seven-circle grid follows this tutorial.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the radius of the first circle, and the unit for every length.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal line, put the compass point on it and draw a circle. Keep the compass at this opening until the end.
Put the compass point where the circle crosses the line on the right and draw a circle through the centre. Do the same on the left. The two new circles touch at the centre.
The two new circles cross the first one at four more points. Draw a circle of the same size around each of them. Six circles now ring the first, and their crossings divide it into six.

Outside the first circle, each pair of neighbouring circles makes a large petal. Rule a line through the centre and the tips of two opposite petals; do it three times. One line is vertical and two lean at 30° either side of it.
The three lines cut the circle at six points. Join them to draw a hexagon standing on a corner; with the six points from the circles, the circle is now divided into twelve.
Join every other corner of the hexagon to draw two triangles, one pointing up and one pointing down. Together they make a six-pointed star.
Join every other one of the six points from the circles to draw a second pair of triangles, pointing right and left. They make a second six-pointed star, turned 30° from the first.

At each point of the first star, rule a line at right angles to the line through the centre, so it just touches the circle. The six lines make a hexagon around the circle: this is the tile, and the next circle sits beyond each of its sides, touching this one at the star's point.

ink.text: Go over the outline of each six-pointed star. Together they make a twelve-pointed star whose two outlines weave through each other.

pattern.text: Repeat the hexagon side to side. Neighbouring stars touch point to point, and the space between three stars stays open.
